mainPoints.title: The Arcade — polish pass
mainPoints.insight: Self-feeding queue — it restarts itself the moment one item ships, no prompt needed.

subtasks.text: Splatflag: fix the infinite-respawn-hit bug
subtasks.note: live 10-15 -- a downed body had no collision for 4 s

subtasks.text: Floor-wide: bring the outline-only games up to the cartoon-outline pass
Arcade lobby: fix choppy main-room movement
Floor-wide: refresh the stale teach-cards
Toy Fury: balance the booster gates
Toy Fury: hazard-variety pass on two tracks
Hangtime: sound rework (verify first)
Floor-wide: ink fix needs more games checked by eye
Splatflag: tutorial covers every mechanic
Skin Kick (AirHockey): fix the ball's look

mainPoints.title: Lobby & controls — getting in and getting out
mainPoints.insight: His first item. Every exit must be impossible to miss.

subtasks.text: Lock the character until Enter is pressed — no running around the lobby before you have entered
Escape menu button (circle with three lines) in ONE corner in every game — Hangtime has it halfway down the screen, Space Golf flips left and right
Replace the small underlined "step away" / "put down the darts" links with a big red LEAVE GAME button

mainPoints.title: Run on a potato — smoothness deep dive
mainPoints.insight: "The main point of this game is to make it super smooth and super optimised and right now it doesn't feel like that."

subtasks.text: Flying around the lobby feels chunky and laggy — find out why and fix it
subtasks.note: live 10-15 — the lobby was never slow while flying (1.1 ms a frame). Your 165 Hz screen was being fed 55 frames a second; flying now gets 82.5. Needs your eyes to confirm

subtasks.text: The shop takes a crazy long time to open — find what it is loading (aura?) and fix it
subtasks.note: live 10-15 — 2.9 s to 0.03 s. Not the aura: it was photographing all 91 skins before showing you anything

subtasks.text: Islands far away drop their props and it looks bad — find the balance between culling and looks
subtasks.note: live 10-15 — island detail switched off at 40 m but the plaza is 48 m away, so every island you could see was a bare deck. 60 m now, priced against 40/60/80: costs 5-8 draw calls

subtasks.text: Toy Fury house: make it insanely well optimized
Deep dive: what it takes for the whole arcade to run on a potato

mainPoints.title: Skins — aura rework
mainPoints.insight: Better than before, still not right. Needs research and a new approach for high-tier skins.

subtasks.text: Aura is still choppy and does not stay with the body moving forward and back; the character leans forward
Aura shows on glasses and items that should not glow — decide what actually earns aura
The aura outline on every skin does not look the best — find a new way to give high-tier skins their aura
Grand Regent: the cape clips into the body and flaps around weirdly
Grand Regent: the player model is broken in the shop
Rename the godly-tier rat to "Pablo" (keep him divine)
Pablo: missing a neck, cheese stuck in his body — redo the whole skin

mainPoints.title: Lobby — center island, bridges & carpets
mainPoints.insight: "I really love the main center island." Keep every table; the connections are what look bad.

subtasks.text: Center island: keep everything (blackjack, roulette, locker), add the small details that make it look a lot better
Bridges to the outer islands land on top of the casino/roulette line — clipping; make the pathways much better
The small red carpets before the jump pads clip over island props
Corner (diagonal) islands connect at random — give them real connecting points that read from a top view
Check every portal: you run through it, never press E
Inside rooms, "Exit" doors are fine where a portal does not fit
Skate park: a skate-park-themed portal instead of the blue one
Toy Fury porch: the giant portal outside does not look good

mainPoints.title: Stardust Cavern tavern — darts & pinball
mainPoints.insight: Anything that costs a coin has to be so fun you cannot decide what to spend your coins on.

subtasks.text: Dartboard is way too big; the cabinet sides clip into the dart scoreboard
Darts: let people play against each other
Darts is too easy — find hard-but-not-impossible; redo the whole dartboard
Pinball: rebuild it into a super fun pinball (2D is fine, dull is not)
Pool balls need numbers and to actually look like pool balls
The pool cue is half the size it should be
Jukebox: touch up the floating music notes
More detail on the bar and the pool table

mainPoints.title: Bowling island
mainPoints.insight: The main idea is good. Inside the alley is fine for now.

subtasks.text: The demo ball crashes the pins every ~5 s — loud and annoying when you stand there; find a better way
Make the demo lane look better
The ball rack and the shoes need a lot more work

mainPoints.title: Slab City — tutorial & trick progression
mainPoints.insight: A wall of controls is overwhelming. Teach the basics first, unlock tricks by levelling. A bigger park comes later.

subtasks.text: A tutorial that walks through the basics of skating, not a wall of controls
An "Open Trick Book" button showing the tricks you have learned so far
Levels that unlock tricks (Skate 3 style: coffin, flips as higher-level moves) and parts of the park
Keep it multiplayer: skate around with others to level up
A stray skating sound plays in the lobby — music, or a leak from the skate park? Find out
Later: grow the park once tricks and basics are in

mainPoints.title: Toy Fury — lobby island & toy house

subtasks.text: Island track: gaps at the turns; cars clip into the track and each other
Cars clip through the loop-de-loop and fall out of it
The toy decorations around the track need a lot more work
The carpet in the main area of the house is broken and clipping
Clipping in almost every room — objects inside objects; build it with more intention
The mini tracks in the house should look like the real race tracks
Shrinking down into a track looks buggy

mainPoints.title: Toy Fury — race revamp
mainPoints.insight: "There's a lot of potential for this game but it just feels like I'm not even really racing."

subtasks.text: Driving: you bounce wall to wall and cannot hold the middle — make it feel like real racing, not just W + A/D
Drop the track picker after you already chose a track (offer mode / race type instead)
Booster pads look like car-wash wipers — redesign them
Wrecks and explosions should be a big part of it — your car can blow up and die
The game looks low resolution — find the cause

mainPoints.title: Toy Fury — car collection
mainPoints.insight: Hot Wheels: collect cars, race the cars you own, spend tickets on cars.

subtasks.text: Design many more car models — spend real time on car design
Collect cars and race the ones you own
Showroom: a motorcycle is upside down; one car already has a driver in it
Wheels turn weirdly and some do not attach to the car; car parts clip

mainPoints.title: Multiplayer — every game
mainPoints.insight: "You're thinking of it from a very narrow lens." Think through the whole party, not one match.

subtasks.text: Pick sides: choose who is on which team
Team sizes beyond 2v2 where the game allows (3v3, 4v4)
"Play again" pulls every player back in
The host chooses whether to fill with bots
Knocked out or finished early: spectate and choose who to watch (Toy Fury, Space Golf), never get thrown to the lobby
Bots wear skins
Cabinets clip a lot, especially the screens
Clean up the cabinets; the hall is a giant box — give it a real vibe
Split it: a single-player room and a multiplayer room
The Splatflag cabinet picture still shows the old map

mainPoints.title: Coins & tickets — find the balance
mainPoints.insight: One coin a game; 100 tickets buys a skin spin. People should be able to spend pretty normally.

subtasks.text: Check daily coins actually refill (a vault note says claim_coins has never paid)
1 coin per game
Vs friends: players put tickets up against each other
Vs bots: the ticket payout scales with bot level
Balance payouts against the 100-ticket spin — lower the spin or raise payouts
A cooler map: lean hard into the cartoony look, with outlines
subtasks.note: Live. Warm cartoon asteroid instead of a flat purple plate, twice-as-thick outlines, pebbles and teal crystals.

subtasks.text: Keep the falling-apart map
subtasks.note: Live. Same rings, bigger fall: the slab about to go sags and glows red-hot, and the one that drops throws dust.

subtasks.text: Bots come in wearing skins
subtasks.note: Live. Nine real shop skins, dealt fresh each match, each bot under its own name.

mainPoints.title: Sideways
mainPoints.insight: A fun single-player start; it belongs in the single-player room.

subtasks.text: The engine revving sound is annoying — rework it
subtasks.note: live 10-15 — it has gears now, so the note drops instead of climbing forever; quiet on a straight, roars when you drift. The siren came down with it.

mainPoints.title: Ice Hockey — make it fun
mainPoints.insight: "I don't want to remove the game. I just want to see how we can make the game better."

subtasks.text: The loop is grab puck, skate to goal, shoot, repeat — deep dive on what would make it fun
Charging a shot looks goofy — make the stick swing look natural
Needs a better name — propose three

mainPoints.title: Broadside Bay (pirate ship) — pivot
mainPoints.insight: Start small, sink ships, grow. No screens that pause the game.

subtasks.text: Start in a small boat; every ship you sink grows yours
Multiplayer: battle other ships to become the biggest (agar.io feel)
Levels from kills upgrade durability, firepower and cannonball capacity
Remove the pause-the-game picks (powder monkeys, chain shot, rum ration)
Remove pressing E to walk around the ship
Keep waves in single-player; aiming can improve later

mainPoints.title: Hangtime — touch-ups
mainPoints.insight: "Otherwise I think this is a fun game."

subtasks.text: A better map: lose the odd background audience and the extra court rings — keep only the 3-point line
Dunking from behind the basket goes through the backboard — block it
A swish sound on a clean 3
Backing up for a 3 sometimes forces a moon dunk instead
Stop asking for a name — use the player's name; signed-out players get "Player 1"
The ball has stars on it — give it a real soccer-ball pattern

mainPoints.title: DodgeFall — both screens must agree, or the game goes
mainPoints.insight: "If we can't figure it out then it's pointless and we'll have to remove the game."

subtasks.text: Deep dive on lag compensation: a kill must be obvious on BOTH screens
If it cannot be solved, removing the game is his call
Freezes when you are about to reach the final green
The camera gets stuck — sometimes you cannot look up or where you want

mainPoints.insight: Kit and demo are built on our end. Every remaining gap is the client's to close, not ours.
